posts.author: Caldus
posts.content_md:
Hi,

I know this may be a bit off-topic, but does anyone here know anything about 3D holography (a volumetric display)? I saw this one video (here it is: [http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FF1vFTQOWN4](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FF1vFTQOWN4)) and now I really want to make something like that. They use some kind of projector, a spinning mirror, a holographic diffuser, and OpenGL graphics on the computer as the subject. I just think it would be really awesome to make something similar. Does anyone know how you would go about making this exactly? Thanks!

posts.author: favalora
posts.content_md:
The movie of a display you referred to was built by researchers out of USC; their SIGGRAPH paper explains how it was made and how it works. My company, [Actuality,](http://www.actuality-medical.com) built a similar system as reported in *Applied Optics*, as well as a commercially-available volumetric display, Perspecta. The nomenclature in the field is still up in the air, but you can call these volumetric displays or multiview volumetric displays, or perhaps even light field displays. There are other ways to make volumetric displays too. But be aware that there are many years' of patents covering these technologies.

-gregg

posts.author: Caldus
posts.content_md: So is it even worth trying to reproduce this? This seems really difficult to do.

posts.author: favalora
posts.content_md:
Hi - 

In my experience, it gets much more difficult as the desired resolution increases. But if you Google around you'll find that a number of high school and college students have built a variety of low-res volumetric displays, many of which periodically sweep a group of LEDs through space.

g
